comment: Settings that Zed tools (zed config, Blueprint) may change. Read by zedcore.registry (validation, UI) and nix/modules/managed.nix (mapping onto NixOS options). Entries of kind 'option' map one-to-one onto the named NixOS option; kind 'special' is interpreted by managed.nix.

settings.title: Boot menu timeout
settings.explain: Seconds the boot menu waits before starting the default generation. Older generations stay selectable in the menu either way; 0 hides the menu unless a key is held.

settings.title: Generations in the boot menu
settings.explain: How many system generations the boot menu lists. Keeping several means you can boot an earlier, known-working system if an update misbehaves.

settings.title: Kernel
settings.explain: default follows the NixOS release's tested kernel (6.18 series in this release). latest is the newest mainline kernel in Zed's pinned package set. lts-6.12 pins the 6.12 long-term-support series, useful for older hardware or out-of-tree drivers.

settings.title: Extra kernel command-line parameters
settings.explain: Parameters appended to the kernel command line, for example 'mitigations=auto' or 'amd_pstate=active'. Wrong parameters can stop the system from booting; earlier generations in the boot menu are unaffected.

settings.title: Swappiness
settings.explain: How eagerly the kernel moves idle memory to swap. Lower values keep applications in RAM longer; the kernel default is 60.

settings.title: NVIDIA driver
settings.explain: nouveau is the free driver and works without network access. proprietary uses NVIDIA's driver (Maxwell to Volta GPUs); proprietary-open uses NVIDIA's driver with its open kernel module (Turing, 2018, and newer). The proprietary variants need 'Allow proprietary software' and are downloaded and built when applied. none: no NVIDIA GPU.

settings.title: Bluetooth
settings.explain: Runs the BlueZ Bluetooth daemon (zed-bluetooth service). Turn it off on machines without Bluetooth or when you do not use it, to reduce attack surface.

settings.title: Power on Bluetooth adapters at boot
settings.explain: When off, Bluetooth adapters stay powered down until you switch them on.

settings.title: CPU frequency governor
settings.explain: Policy the kernel uses to scale CPU frequency. Unset leaves the driver's default. 'performance' keeps clocks high at the cost of power; 'powersave' on intel_pstate/amd_pstate still scales dynamically.

settings.title: Graphical desktop
settings.explain: The Zed desktop: Wayland sessions on seatd, the greetd login screen, PipeWire audio, the Zed panel and lock screen, all supervised by s6. Turning it off leaves a text-console system.

settings.title: Desktop sessions
settings.explain: Sessions offered on the login screen; install several and choose at login. labwc: stacking windows (default). niri: scrollable tiling. sway: i3-style tiling. docs/DESKTOPS.md lists what each is verified to do on Zed and why GNOME and Plasma are not offered.

settings.title: Keyboard layout
settings.explain: XKB layout name(s) used by the desktop, such as 'us' or 'de,us'. The console keymap is set separately.

settings.title: Host name
settings.explain: The machine's name on the local network. It is visible to other devices on networks you join and in DHCP requests.

settings.title: Wi-Fi MAC address
settings.explain: random uses a new hardware address for every connection, so networks cannot recognise the device across visits. stable keeps one address per network. permanent always uses the adapter's burned-in address. Some captive portals and MAC-filtered networks need 'stable' or 'permanent'.

settings.title: Ethernet MAC address
settings.explain: Same choices as for Wi-Fi, applied to wired connections.

settings.title: Firewall
settings.danger: Turning the firewall off exposes every listening service to the networks this machine joins.
settings.explain: The nftables firewall drops unsolicited incoming connections. It is loaded fail-closed: if the ruleset cannot be applied, networking does not start.

settings.title: Open TCP ports
settings.explain: Incoming TCP ports accepted from any network. Only open ports for services you run and intend to reach from other machines.

settings.title: Open UDP ports
settings.explain: Incoming UDP ports accepted from any network.

settings.title: Log refused connections
settings.explain: Writes a kernel log line for every dropped connection attempt. Useful for diagnosis; noisy on busy networks.

settings.title: SSH server
settings.danger: Enabling the SSH server lets other machines attempt to log in. Use key-based authentication.
settings.explain: OpenSSH server (zed-sshd service). NixOS opens its port in the firewall automatically while it is enabled.

settings.title: SSH password logins
settings.explain: When off, only key-based logins are accepted, which resists password guessing.

settings.title: Tor daemon
settings.explain: Runs a system Tor daemon (zed-tor service). On its own this routes nothing: applications must be configured to use it. Tor Browser bundles its own Tor and does not need this.

settings.title: Tor SOCKS client port
settings.explain: Offers Tor's SOCKS proxy on 127.0.0.1:9050 for applications that you configure to use it.

settings.title: Services not started at boot
settings.explain: s6-rc services removed from the boot bundle. They stay installed and can be started by hand with 'zed services start NAME'. Core services that the system cannot boot without are refused.

settings.title: Time zone
settings.explain: IANA time zone, for example 'Europe/Berlin'.

settings.title: System language
settings.explain: Locale for messages, dates and number formats, for example 'en_US.UTF-8'.

settings.title: Console keymap
settings.explain: Keyboard layout for text consoles (tty1-6 and the recovery console on tty9).

settings.title: Privacy profile
settings.explain: standard: firewall on, nothing listening, no telemetry. private: additionally randomises MAC addresses, disables Bluetooth power-on, hides the host name from DHCP and turns on IPv6 privacy addresses. custom: no profile changes; use the individual settings. No profile makes the machine anonymous; see Zed Veil for Tor and isolated workspaces.

settings.title: sudo asks for a password
settings.danger: Without a password, any program running as an administrator account can become root silently.
settings.explain: Whether members of the wheel group must enter their password for sudo.

settings.title: Process tracing restriction
settings.explain: Yama ptrace scope. 1 (Zed's default) lets a process debug only its own children; 0 allows any same-user process, which some debuggers and reverse-engineering tools expect; 2 limits tracing to root; 3 disables it entirely until reboot.

settings.title: Parallel Nix builds
settings.explain: How many derivations Nix builds at the same time during updates and installs.

settings.title: CPU cores per build
settings.explain: Cores each build may use. 0 means all cores.

settings.title: Allow proprietary software
settings.explain: Lets Zed Arsenal and 'zed install' install packages whose licence is not free (for example some drivers and Burp Suite). Their licence is always shown before installation.
